prerequisites: Completion of all other courses required for the Mechanical Engineering degree

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to prepare an original individual exercise to be presented and defended before a university tribunal, consisting of a project in the field of specific technologies of Industrial Engineering of a professional nature in which the competencies acquired in the degree are synthesized and integrated.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering that have as their object, in accordance with the knowledge acquired as established in section 5 of Order CIN/351/2009 of February 9, the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in HA_21.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan within a company and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

Democratic values and sustainability. Develop a commitment to the society in which we live for it to prosper through the dimensions of democratic values and sustainability, materialized within the global framework that defines it at all times.
Teamwork. Actively collaborate with a group of people to achieve a common goal by combining different talents.
Critical thinking. Reason reflectively about a topic, being able to deliberate on its validity by subjecting one's own and external convictions to debate.
Emotional intelligence. Understand and regulate one's own and others' emotions to interact and participate effectively and constructively in social and professional life.
Innovation and Creativity. Design and carry out a new task or project differently, using creativity and curiosity to add value with an entrepreneurial attitude.

Permanent self-learning. Use continuous learning and develop autonomous and flexible learning strategies throughout life to be part of an active, motivated, and integrated citizenry, promoting job improvement or personal development.

teaching_methods: Regular meetings to monitor work and resolve doubts

assessment_methods.method: Quality and depth of the work itself
Evaluation by the director(s) and, if applicable, the rapporteur, in their report

assessment_rules: After the defense of the Final Degree Project (TFG), the tribunal members must issue an individual evaluation report, from which the final grade will be assigned. In case of a failing evaluation, the tribunal must issue a report detailing the deficiencies, both methodological and content-related, that justify said grade. This report will also indicate the modifications that need to be introduced into the work, and a new defense will proceed. The transversal competencies 'Emotional Intelligence' and 'Innovation and Creativity' will be evaluated by the tribunal based on the report and the presentation of the work.
